div.head: III Eg 8.2
div.ab: ⁊ ga seo wæg wulle to ealfan punde, ⁊ hie nan man ná deoror ne sylle.
⁊ ga seo wæge wulle to CXX, ⁊ nan man hy na undeoror ne sylle.
And ga seo wæge wulle to CXX p', ⁊ nan man hig undeoror ne sille.
⁊ ga seo wæge wulle to healfan punde, ⁊ nan man hy na undeoror ne sylle.
Et eat pondus lane pro dimidia libra, et nemo carius uendat eam.
⁊ ga seo wæge wulle to CXX p', ⁊ nan man hig undeoror ne sille.
And ga seo wæg wulle to healfan punde, and hie nan man na undeoror ne sylle.
Und es gehe das ‘Gewicht’ [etwa 1½ Centner?] Wolle zu ½ Pfund (= 120 Pfennigen A D) Silber, und es verkaufe sie niemand billiger (theurer G Qu).
And let a ‘wey’ [about 1½ hundredweight?] of wool go for ½ pound (= 120 pence, A D) of silver, and let no one sell it more cheaply (more dearly, G Qu).
And a wey of wool shall be sold for 120 pence, and no-one shall sell it at a cheaper rate.
And a wey of wool is to be sold at half a pound, and no one is to sell it more dearly.
And a wey of wool is to be valued at half a pound, and no one may sell it for a lower price.
div.note: ‘p'’ is supplied in A from D. G's ‘deoror’ should be corrected to ‘undeoror’ (A, D, G2). In G a blank line follows, then in the same hand the rubrics of Alfred (above, p. 16). Co cites 8.2 ‘de legibus Eadgari, ut apud S. Augustinum extra Cantuariam inueni’. G2: the ‘l’ of ‘healfan’ is written above the line.; AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 358 / 359, October 2026 (was “∅”, now “|”)
wey: A unit of weight for dry goods that varied over time, though a wool wey was typically the equivalent of approximately two hundred pounds.
half a pound: One hundred twenty shillings.

Vgl. Gl Wolle 1. Unmöglich kann das provinzielle Gewicht weight (Wright Dial. dict.) zu 32 Engl. Pfund gemeint sein, weil dann 1 Pfund Wolle 4 Pf. kosten würde
Cf. Gl Wolle 1. The provincial weight weight (Wright Dial. dict.) of 32 English pounds cannot possibly be meant, because then 1 pound of wool would cost 4 pence
p' kommt häufig vor als Abkürzung für pening (s. d. Wb), aber nie (wie Price meinte) für pund. Die Hss. variieren also hierin nicht inhaltlich
p' occurs frequently as an abbreviation for pening (see that word in Wb), but never (as Price thought) for pund. The MSS therefore do not differ in substance here

‘fester Mindestpreis für einen Ausfuhrartikel zu dieser alten Zeit merkwürdig’; Cunningham Entwi. d. Industrie (Dt. 1912) 152. Auch Stone in Law Quart. Rev. 1913, 323 versteht Minimum. Als Käufer kann recht wohl auch der Weber des Inlands gedacht sein

‘a fixed minimum price for an export article is remarkable at this early period’; Cunningham Entwi. d. Industrie (German ed. 1912) 152. Stone in Law Quart. Rev. 1913, 323 also understands a minimum. The native weaver too may very well be envisaged as a buyer
The standard of the wey appears to have varied somewhat, both in the Anglo-Saxon period and later, see Harmer, op. cit. p. 73; Cunningham, Growth of Industry, p. 130; Bateson, E.H.R., 1899, p. 505.
deoror, G, Q. Cunningham, loc. cit. and Stone (L.Q.R., 1913, p. 338) accept undeoror (the reading of the second recension) and regard this regulation as the earliest fixing a minimum price for wool.

note.label: dearly
note.seg: Liebermann takes this as an error for undeoror “more cheaply”, the reading of the Wulfstan MSS, but it is supported by Quadripartitus, and may be the original text. The position may have changed by the time the alteration was made.
